title: Quadratic normal errors and removal of a boundary regularizer
reviewed_arguments: All 33 original obligations, 27 displays, three complete solutions and the original diagram are retained.
Both actual weak form domains, the full complex lower terms, exact tester orders and fixed-width constants are retained.
The separated-pair lemma moves only actual b-coefficient adjoints, with at most one ordinary derivative on each input.
The quadratic identity includes all three negative tails; each has a bare-energy bound using uniform residual coefficients.
The positive-order parametrix identity passes to weak solutions by form-space density and distributional continuity.
The matrix principal root is an ordered convergent series; every derivative is controlled without commuting matrix derivatives.
The scalar coefficient recurrence proves the square identity; actual quantization keeps the complete order-minus-one remainder.
The balanced pair at target nu-1 uses the exact nu-3/2 input tester and controls the lower remainder.
The full complex quadratic norm has leading omega/epsilon, hence delta at corrected glancing support, with the explicit Young remainder.
Finite block reuse is conditional on the combined normal estimate; no physical-corner analytic input is asserted.
Every regularizer derivative has its explicit polynomial form, uniform order-zero bound, fixed-r negative order and sqrt(r) order-one rate.
Fixed compact base localization precedes lacunary convolution, whose constant limit gives the actual multiplication operator chi.
Uniform energy maps and positive-order estimates yield strong convergence on both form domains; individual Br and adjoint tests are legal.
Supported transpose actions agree with zero extensions of L2 outputs by density. Tests nonzero at the boundary identify the full supported limit.
Rational-step density, H1 closed-graph completeness, Gram–Schmidt, nested-square subsequences and diagonal extraction prove the Hilbert norm limit.
Hilbert representation converts every supported test pairing to a weak functional; the limit equals Bu0 without discarding boundary terms.
The limit keeps the precise norm supplied and the fixed-width order of limits; a variable-coefficient commutator is not assumed zero.
The three complete exercise solutions, five finite model groups and original figure are checked; finite computations do not replace analytic proofs.
